# GenData — AI-Powered Synthetic Data Generation

A full-stack platform that generates realistic, privacy-safe synthetic datasets for ML training, analytics, testing, and research — across healthcare, finance, agriculture, cybersecurity, e-commerce, and more.

Instead of generating generic fake rows, GenData either **extracts real structure from your own documents** (PDFs, reports, images, invoices, CSVs) and generates synthetic data that mirrors it, or lets you **describe a dataset in plain English** and turns that prompt into a full schema and dataset — with privacy checks and quality scoring built in.

Built with **Next.js** on the frontend and **FastAPI (Python)** on the backend.

---

## Features

### Two Ways to Generate Data
- **Extraction-based generation** — upload a PDF, invoice, medical report, image, or CSV; the system extracts structure and content, then generates a synthetic dataset that mirrors the real patterns without exposing the original data.
- **Prompt/schema-based generation** — describe what you want in natural language, pick a template, or define a schema directly; an LLM converts the prompt into a structured generation spec (columns, types, constraints) before generating rows.

### Domain-Aware Generation (7 domains)
Healthcare, finance, agriculture, cybersecurity, e-commerce, text analytics, and general ML tabular/text datasets — each with its own schema definitions, formatters, and post-processing rules (e.g. finance transactions get realistic amount distributions, healthcare gets clinically-consistent lab values).

### Hybrid Generation Engine
Rather than relying on one method, generation blends three approaches depending on the domain and data available:
- **LLM-based row generation** (Groq-hosted Llama models) for realistic, context-aware content
- **SDV (Synthetic Data Vault)** — statistical/generative modeling learned from a reference dataset, with domain-specific post-processing for finance, healthcare, e-commerce, cybersecurity, and ML data
- **Rule engine + Faker**, including a locale-aware generator for realistic **Indian names, phone numbers, cities, and addresses** — plus a correlated-field generator so related columns (e.g. age ↔ occupation) stay logically consistent
- A **reference-data learner** that auto-detects the domain of an uploaded CSV and learns its statistical patterns to extend into new synthetic rows

### Real Computer-Vision & Medical AI (not just LLM wrappers)
- **Plant disease detection** — a locally-run EfficientNet-B3 model (trained on PlantVillage, 38 disease classes) analyzes crop images and returns a diagnosis plus treatment recommendations, for agriculture-domain extraction.
- **Chest X-ray / medical image analysis** — TorchXRayVision (DenseNet-121) classifies pathologies from medical images; the model is pre-warmed at server startup so the first real request isn't slow.
- **Healthcare OCR + RAG** — a dedicated document extractor pulls text from medical reports/scans, chunks it, and retrieves relevant context to ground diagnosis verification and risk assessment.
- **Medical risk engine** — assesses extracted lab values/entities and flags risk levels.

### AI Prompt Intelligence
- Prompt-to-schema conversion with domain auto-detection
- Dynamic schema inference from natural language
- A dedicated "generate/prompt/v2" flow that also accepts file uploads alongside a prompt

### Validation, Privacy & Quality
- **PII detection** via Microsoft Presidio (with an automatic regex-based fallback if Presidio/spaCy isn't available), so sensitive data never leaks into "synthetic" output
- Responsible-AI checks and dataset quality scoring (a dedicated metrics engine + quality report)
- Schema and row-count validation against the generation spec
- A `/verify-diagnosis` endpoint for validating AI-generated healthcare diagnoses

### Auth, Export & Dashboard
- **Clerk-based authentication** (JWT verification via JWKS) protecting API access, with a dev-mode bypass flag for local testing
- Dataset export to CSV, Excel, and JSON, plus PDF report generation for healthcare and agriculture datasets
- An overview dashboard tracking recent datasets, recent activity, usage stats, and available templates

### Reliability
- **3-tier LLM fallback**: Groq (fast hosted inference) → local Ollama models, so generation keeps working if the hosted API is rate-limited or down
- Rate limiting via SlowAPI to protect the backend from abuse

---

## Architecture

```
User
 │
 ▼
Frontend (Next.js) — Login/Sign-up, Dashboard, File Upload, Reports, Exports
 │  HTTP/JSON
 ▼
Authentication Layer — Clerk JWT verification, role access
 │
 ▼
FastAPI Backend — API routes, business services, request validation
 │
 ├── Extractors ──────── OCR · Vision analysis (plant disease, X-ray) · Document parsing
 ├── Prompt Engine ────── Domain detection · Schema building · Prompt formatting
 └── Generation Engine ── LLM generation · SDV · Faker · Rule engine
        │
        ▼
   LLM Client — Groq (text + vision) · Ollama fallback · TorchXRayVision (DenseNet)
        │
        ▼
   Validation, Quality & Privacy Layer — Schema check · Row-count check · Quality score · PII scan (Presidio)
        │
        ▼
   Database & File Storage — Users · Sessions · Uploaded files · Generated datasets
        │
        ▼
   Output — Dashboard view · CSV/Excel/JSON export · PDF reports
```

---

## Tech Stack

**Frontend**
- Next.js 14 / React 18, Tailwind CSS
- `@clerk/nextjs` for authentication
- `@tanstack/react-table` for dataset previews
- `xlsx` for client-side spreadsheet handling

**Backend**
- FastAPI + Uvicorn, SlowAPI for rate limiting
- Groq API (Llama models, text + vision) with local Ollama fallback
- SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) + Faker for statistical/rule-based generation
- Presidio (analyzer + anonymizer) + spaCy for PII detection, with regex fallback
- PyTorch, torchvision, timm — EfficientNet-B3 for plant disease classification
- TorchXRayVision — DenseNet-121 for medical image pathology analysis
- PyMuPDF, pdfminer.six, pdfplumber, pytesseract, pdf2image — document/OCR extraction
- python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl — multi-format file parsing
- ReportLab — PDF report generation
- PyJWT + cryptography + bcrypt — auth/token handling

---

## Getting Started

### Frontend
```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). You'll need Clerk API keys in `frontend/.env.local` (`NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`).

### Backend
```bash
cd backend
pip install -r requirements.txt
python run.py
```
- Swagger UI: [http://localhost:8000/docs](http://localhost:8000/docs)
- Set `GROQ_API_KEY` in `backend/.env` (and optionally point to a local Ollama instance as fallback)
- For local dev without Clerk configured, set `APP_ENV=development` and `ALLOW_DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=true`

First run will download the EfficientNet-B3 and TorchXRayVision model weights automatically (via `timm`/`torchxrayvision`).

---

## Key API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/extract` | Upload and extract structured data from a file |
| `POST /api/extract/agriculture/bulk` | Bulk agriculture image extraction (plant disease detection) |
| `POST /api/generate` | Generate a synthetic dataset from an extraction session |
| `POST /api/generate/prompt/v2` | Generate a dataset from a natural-language prompt |
| `POST /api/generate/prompt/v2/upload` | Prompt + file upload combined generation |
| `POST /api/generate/prompt/excel` \| `/csv` | Generate and export directly to Excel/CSV |
| `POST /verify-diagnosis` | Validate an AI-generated healthcare diagnosis |
| `POST /api/evaluate` | Evaluate dataset quality |
| `GET /api/datasets/` | List generated datasets |
| `GET /api/export/{dataset_id}` | Export a dataset |
| `DELETE /api/datasets/{dataset_id}` | Delete a dataset |
| `GET /api/overview/stats` \| `/recent-datasets` \| `/recent-activities` \| `/templates` | Dashboard analytics |
| `GET /health` | Health check |

---

## Project Structure

```
├── frontend/                      # Next.js app (Clerk auth, dashboard, extraction UI, exports)
├── backend/
│   ├── run.py                      # Entry point (uvicorn)
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py                 # FastAPI app + route registration
│   │   ├── auth.py                 # Clerk JWT verification
│   │   ├── generator.py            # Core generation orchestration
│   │   ├── reference_data_learner.py
│   │   ├── rule_engine.py          # Rule-based generation logic
│   │   ├── privacy.py              # Presidio-based PII detection
│   │   ├── correlated_generator.py # Locale-aware, correlated field generation
│   │   ├── engines/                # SDV, hybrid, EfficientNet, quality/metrics engines
│   │   ├── healthcare/             # OCR, RAG, risk engine, PDF export for medical data
│   │   └── routes/                 # extract, generate, generate_v2, export, overview, verify
│   ├── extractors/                 # Domain-specific extractors (agriculture, finance, healthcare, text)
│   ├── pdf_reports/                 # Standalone PDF report builders
│   └── tests/                       # Backend test suite
```

---

## Known Limitations

- Session data is stored in memory and doesn't persist across restarts without a full database setup.
- Depends on external AI APIs (Groq) — performance and availability vary with API rate limits and network latency.
- Healthcare workflows (OCR + vision + RAG) are more resource-intensive and slower than tabular generation.
- Deployment
- Large file uploads and dataset generation increase CPU/memory usage significantly.

## Future Enhancements

- Support for additional LLM providers (GPT, Claude, Gemini) for model redundancy
- Full cloud-based architecture for scalability
- Domain-specific model upgrades for agriculture and healthcare extraction accuracy
